summary: Tencent's fast, dependency-free neural network inference engine for running AI models on phones, PCs, browsers and edge devices.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ncnn is a high-performance inference framework for running trained neural networks on mobile, embedded and desktop devices. It is pure C++ with no third-party runtime dependencies, runs on CPUs (with ARM NEON optimizations) and on GPUs through Vulkan, and has a C API and Python binding. The pnnx tool converts PyTorch and ONNX models to ncnn's format, and it supports fp16, int8 quantization and custom layers.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running AI models on phones and small devices needs a small, fast runtime. ncnn provides one without heavy dependencies.
whoFor: Engineers deploying vision models on edge devices
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for lightweight on-device inference with Vulkan GPU support and an easy PyTorch-to-ncnn path.
requirements: Python with PyTorch (for converting models with pnnx)
CMake and a C++ compiler (to build from source)

overview: The recommended beginner path is PyTorch to pnnx to ncnn: install pnnx with pip3 install pnnx and export your model.
Export produces model.ncnn.param and model.ncnn.bin, which you load with the C++ API or the Python binding.
Use the prebuilt packages when possible, or build from source with CMake for Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS or WebAssembly. BSD 3-Clause licensed.
limitations: Only operators ncnn supports can be converted
Building from source for each platform takes setup
